core.text: Commit early to the selection-reordering account: the stipulated miswrite occurs when refresh changes the key occupying a retained selected row. This is the best main mechanism for the supplied trace; wider causal sufficiency remains a hypothesis.

Adopt one operating construction: keep S0 loaded throughout three sequential inspect/select-and-commit pairs. Inspect/select K2 during 0-1, commit during 1-2; inspect/select K5 during 2-3, commit during 3-4; inspect/select K7 during 4-5, commit during 5-6. Perform the sole refresh during 6-7. Do not insert intermediate refreshes or mismatch correction loops.

Prospective model prediction: selections remain rows 2, 5 and 7 until their commits, so writes target K2, K5 and K7 only. The final refresh should load S2 while preserving statuses by key, leaving precisely those targets checked and five others unchecked. Source scores remain read-only. This seven-minute success has not been observed.

Verify the proposed replay by logging each action time, loaded snapshot, retained row, intended key and actual written key. Acceptance requires zero incorrect-key writes, including repaired writes; exactly three target corrections; unchanged source scores; final S2 loaded; and completion within ten minutes. Any violation rejects this construction for the stipulated outcome.

residue.text: The equal score 75 for K5 and K7 prevents score-only identification. Verify final statuses against explicit immutable keys. The anomaly reinforces identity checks without establishing intermediate freshness necessity.

Only one wrong-target write is stipulated. Repeated mismatch-triggered refresh feedback remains unobserved and is outside the committed construction. If investigated later, changing/frozen snapshots crossed with row/key binding could distinguish initial reordering from recurrence; their results remain hypotheses.

Claims concern eight invented records only. Real selection binding, detection and interruption costs are unknown; concurrency, deleted keys and load failures are excluded. No production reliability, operational savings or human benefit follows from the proposed synthetic replay.
